Recife grew around the water. The Capibaribe River, canals, and bridges divide the city center into distinct areas, which is why Recife is often compared to Venice. A walk through the city can easily be combined with time on the Atlantic coast.

The historic neighborhoods preserve buildings dating from the Portuguese and Dutch periods, including churches, mansions, and other old architecture. A city itinerary can take in this part of Recife, its local cultural scene, restaurants, and waterfront walks.

Recife makes a convenient first stop on a journey through northeastern Brazil. From here, it is natural to continue to Olinda and Porto de Galinhas, with Fernando de Noronha as an addition to a longer itinerary.

The architecture is another reason to visit: neighboring tombs differ in their facades, materials, and artistic decoration. A visit can easily be combined with the Basilica of Our Lady of Pilar and a walk through the Recoleta neighborhood itself; admission conditions should be confirmed before arriving.
